prompt:
I need the front end for CloseOut. An internal work-planning tool built by a hospital system's finance IT group, used by the payroll department to schedule recurring close cycles around staff availability and hard regulatory dates.

Who's using it: Marguerite Lacroix, payroll operations manager at a 9,400-employee regional hospital network. She leads a team of 11 payroll specialists and has run year-end close six times.

What they're doing right now: It is late November and she is putting together the year-end close plan for December 1 to January 16. W-2 file delivery, the final 2026 bonus run, benefit deduction changes taking effect January 1, and the first payroll of 2027 all fall within the same weeks as holiday PTO. Two specialists have requested Dec 22 to Jan 2 off, and the department's most experienced tax specialist goes on leave January 5. She is assigning the 46 close tasks to people and dates, respecting dependencies and the bank's ACH cutoff times, and making sure at least two qualified people are covering each critical day before she circulates the plan to the team and the controller on Monday.

What's in the system at this point: 46 year-end tasks, each with an estimated effort (0.5–3 days), a required skill (tax, garnishments, benefits, bonus processing, reconciliation), dependencies (e.g. 'Final bonus import' must precede 'Bonus tax true-up'), and fixed deadlines (Dec 19 bonus pay date, Dec 31 final payroll check date, Jan 9 W-2 vendor file, Jan 15 first 2027 payroll). 11 team members with skill tags and approved/requested PTO (e.g. Dev Patel off Dec 22–Jan 2, Carla Mendes leave starting Jan 5). Hospital holidays: Dec 25, Jan 1. Bank ACH cutoff 3:00 pm ET, two business days before pay date. Biweekly pay dates: Dec 5, Dec 19, Jan 2, Jan 16. Last year's plan is attached for reference, with 7 tasks that ran late.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
